_notes: HOW EACH MISSION MODULE IS TAUGHT (docs/design/minigames.md).
Owner pass 2026-08-09: three of the five modules 'make no sense, need a
tutorial'. The one-page blurbs in lessons.json are flavour; they never
said what a clue counts, what a break in a thread means, or what a gust
does.
Owner pass 2026-08-13 rewrote three of these where the BOARD changed
under them: the Unpicking no longer colours its free threads in (it
stacks them, and only the first lattice tags them), the crossing posts
an obstacle instead of a bare humour, and the ward hands a card back
when a patch comes up. A lesson describing an older board is worse than
no lesson.
These play as coach marks over the REAL board (ui/coach.gd), the same
overlay the prologue's battle uses. A step with no `wait` is a note:
tapping anywhere advances it. A step with `wait: true` only advances
when the player performs the action, and its target must therefore be
something they can always do (law 17) -- which is why the action steps
spotlight the whole board rather than one edge or one thread.
Targets are resolved by each screen:
''             -- no spotlight; a note in the middle of the page
'board'        -- the whole drawn board
'board:<key>'  -- an invisible marker the screen lays over a feature
anything else  -- a real button on the page (squint, turn, press...)
A module plays its tutorial once, on first sight, and its '?' button
replays it forever after. `stitch_mirror` REPLACES `stitch` on a
mirrored chart -- the Ch3 payoff needs its own rule said out loud.

steps.text: A seam is ONE closed loop of thread. One. No loose ends, and never two circles.
Every number counts the stitches that touch its square. A 2 wants exactly two of that square's four sides sewn — no more.
Tap between two dots to sew. Tap a stitch again to take it out. Unpicking is free: nothing here punishes thinking twice.
A number turns GREEN and takes a ring when it has exactly what it asked for. It turns RED when you have given it too much.
Stuck? SQUINT costs a paw and tells the truth: a stitch to take out, a gap the seam runs through, or both.
Answer every number AND close the loop — they are two rules, not one. Get the numbers right with the thread still open and the seam will tell you what is missing.
You have sewn this before. The rules have not changed: one closed loop, every number answered.
The CLUES have. They are pinned on backward, as if read in a glass — the number at the far left belongs to the square at the far RIGHT.
So a number lights green when the square it truly belongs to is satisfied, not the one it is sitting over. Follow the colour, not the position.
Ash's paw finds this easier than it should. That is the part he thinks about afterward.
A ward is a promise stitched into a doorway. This one tore, and the night is already leaning on it.
The dark squares are the tear. Every square you cover is a draft that does not get in.
There is no basket of patches. There is your spool. DRAW takes the next card off it and spends it — and hands you whatever cloth that card cuts.

The humour is the shape of the cut and the worth is its size. Ferocity cuts long strips, guile cuts crooked ones, shadow cuts squares, and Moonlight cuts the small strange piece that finishes a corner.
DRAG the cloth onto the ward. Tap a patch already down to pick it back up — moving cloth costs nothing. Only drawing does.
TURN IT swings the piece a quarter at a time. Watch its own picture on the card: that is where the turn shows.
Patches may sit on top of each other and may hang over sound cloth. Nobody is grading the neatness — only the squares still OPEN count against you.
So the only real question is how many more cards you are willing to spend here. Every one you draw is one the next fight will not have; every square still open follows you into it.
Somebody wove this shut, and did it well. You are taking it apart one thread at a time without letting the whole thing seize.
The threads lie in a stack. One with nothing crossing over the top of it is loose — follow it end to end and see.
A thread that passes UNDER another is in its shadow where they cross, and the one on top runs unbroken across it. That shadow is the whole puzzle: it says which is holding which down.
Pull a loose thread. Tap it once and it slides out.
Pull a trapped one and the lattice twangs: it and everything lying across it shiver, and the ALARM climbs. Fill the pips and you are heard.
Some workings argue back. Take one thread and another snaps across its neighbour — it trembles BLUE when it does. Read it again before you pull.
This first working tags its loose threads in brass, and so does this lesson whenever you replay it. No other working will. After tonight you read the stack yourself.
Nothing to fight here. Same paw, same spool, same spent pile — a different question: what does it cost to get across?
Something is in the road. There will be a few of these between here and the door, and each one is its own decision.
Every way past it is priced: what ENERGY it wants, and how much of it. Tap a way to choose it.
Then put cards on it. Tap a card to lay it down, tap it again to take it back. Worth is what counts, not how many cards — and Moonlight pays for anything.
GO takes the way you chose. Pay in full and you are past it clean; the cards are spent either way, and stay spent into whatever comes after tonight.
You may go SHORT. Nothing here refuses you — but the button tells you the odds first, and if the street collects, it collects in health.
READ AHEAD spends a paw to see what is round the next corner, so you can keep something back for it.
Tap the spool up top to count what is left to draw. Or TURN BACK, and the long way home becomes the very long way home.
Ash cannot question a person — to them he is a cat on a wall. Animals are another matter. They will talk to him about people all night.
Each band is something the witness said. Tap one to PRESS it — they elaborate, and now and then say more than they meant to. A band you have pressed goes pale.
Tap a thing in the Casebook to read what you wrote about it, then hold it up. With it in your paw, tap the band it breaks.
A wrong accusation spends patience. Run it out and they stop talking — the lead goes on, just poorer.
A band you can already disprove wears a loose thread. You will never have to guess at one you cannot break yet.
